title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: When a fortress compounder trades at a market multiple while coiling right on its rising 30-week moving average, you do not wait for perfection—you size the asymmetry and respect the stop.
epigraph.author: Executive Underwriting Thesis

web_blocks.html: What JPMorgan Chase Does & Why It Compounds: JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM) is the premier universal bank in the United States. In FY2025, it generated $182.45 billion in GAAP net revenue ($185.6B managed) and $57.05 billion in net income [1]. That output produced a 20% ROTCE on a 14.6% Standardized CET1 ratio [1]. In Q3 2026, it sustained 20% reported ROTCE (21% adjusted) on 13.9% CET1 [3]. Three core pillars drive this flywheel. Consumer & Community Banking delivered $76.0B in FY2025 revenue across 5,000+ branches and 75M+ digital users [1, 10]. Commercial & Investment Bank earned $28.0B in net income on $78.5B of revenue [1]. Asset & Wealth Management added $24.1B in revenue across $7T in client assets [1, 12]. Together, they compounded Tangible Book Value Per Share from $51.44 in 2016 to $107.56 in 2025 (8.5% CAGR) alongside a ~1.82% dividend yield [1, 20].

Dual Verdict & Three-Horizon Opportunity Matrix: Our isolated price-blind audit rated business quality as COMPOUNDER_PASS with kpi_health: PASS. At the verified November 13, 2026 close of $346.19 (14.52x TTM P/E on $23.84 EPS, 3.22x FY25 TBV), we assign a new-capital verdict of WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2, CORE_ALPHA) [20, 21]. Reverse DCF shows $346.19 prices in ~17.5% normalized ROTCE, close to management's 17% cycle target [4]. Technically, JPM sits in Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) with a flat-to-falling 50-day SMA ($340.42) during a broader market Correction [21, 27]. At $346.19, CMP reward-to-risk is 1.77:1 (+12.10% to $388.09 vs. -6.84% to $322.51). Waiting for a pullback into the $326.16–$335.05 support zone improves asymmetry to 4.23:1 [21]. Per the November 13, 2026 US positions ledger, JPM is NOT currently held (holding_action: NOT_HELD, holding_shares_to_sell: 0), so 100% of the $3,818.88 marginal US cash unit stays in reserve until JPM tests $326.16–$335.05 [27].

web_blocks.html: Key Risks & What Would Change Our Mind: Our underwriting weighs four Bear risks against this thesis. First, faster U.S. labor softening could push Card Services NCOs well above management's ~3.2%–3.4% outlook [3]. Second, Basel III Endgame and G-SIB capital rules could inflate risk-weighted assets and cap ROE [14]. Third, opaque private credit funds could trigger systemic liquidity spillovers [17]. Fourth, post-Jamie Dimon CEO succession could test cultural execution [18]. We would downgrade immediately on a weekly close below $322.51, a CET1 drop below 13.0%, or Card NCOs breaching 4.0%. Investors should wait for $326.16–$335.05 support and track quarterly credit provisioning closely.

book_paragraphs: Every serious investment decision boils down to two questions: is this a business worth owning through a full economic cycle, and is the market offering you an asymmetric price to step aboard today? On JPMorgan Chase & Co., after a two-pass audit that deliberately separated business forensics from the stock quote, our answer to both questions is a clear, unhedged yes.

JPMorgan Chase is not just America's largest bank; it is a $182.45 billion revenue machine that converted crisis-era rescues—Bear Stearns and Washington Mutual in 2008, First Republic in 2023—into an unmatched coast-to-coast deposit and wealth franchise. Across its Consumer, Commercial & Investment Bank, and $7 trillion Asset & Wealth Management divisions, it earned $57.05 billion in 2025 (20% ROTCE) and more than doubled Tangible Book Value Per Share over the past decade.

At $346.19 (14.52x trailing TTM earnings, 3.22x FY25 TBV), the stock is not priced for perfection; our Reverse DCF shows Wall Street already assumes ROTCE fades toward 17.5%. However, the chart sits in Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) with a flat-to-falling 50-day moving average ($340.42) during a broader market Correction, leaving only 1.77:1 reward-to-risk at CMP. Waiting for a pullback into $326.16–$335.05 lifts asymmetry to 4.23:1 against our $322.51 stop. Since we hold zero shares (NOT_HELD), JPM earns WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT for marginal US cash.

Across the ten chapters ahead, you and I will examine every piece of evidence from first principles—starting with how JPMorgan turned the 2008 and 2023 banking panics into permanent market-share step-changes, walking through concrete customer examples inside every business line, auditing management's 3-to-5-year track record, and stress-testing both the Bull and Bear cases against today's exact price.

Just as important, we will not sweep the Bear case under the rug. We will examine credit card delinquency normalization, Basel III Endgame capital rules, private credit shadow-banking risks, and the inevitable post-Dimon succession question—so that if you commit capital to JPMorgan Chase, you know every risk on the ledger and the exact $322.51 line in the sand where our thesis is invalidated. Let us open the ledger and walk through the full institutional case together, one chapter at a time, with complete transparency on both the numbers and the judgment calls, so you can size and execute with confidence.
